record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Gap scaling of deformed activity/current evolution operators
record.original_question: For the deformed Markov matrices that bias exclusion-process trajectories by current or activity, can the spectral gap be computed by Bethe Ansatz near dynamical phase transitions and for nonzero Legendre parameters? In particular, under the mapping between the SSEP activity-biased operator M and the ASEP current-biased operator W, does the gap of M scale as L^{-3/2} for sufficiently large |s|, which would imply dynamical exponent 3/2 for SSEP activity large deviations beyond the diffusive regime?

evidence.quote:
Last, studies of the gap in the deformed
evolution operator (which is in principle possible within the Bethe Ansatz approach) could shed light
on the ﬁnite-time scalings close to a DPT, in the spirit of previous works in diﬀusive [123] and super-
diﬀusive [124] models, or in so-called large- N models [55,125].

It would be
interesting to extend their computation to the case of the deformed Markov matrices we have considered.
For instance, if through the mapping between M and W , the gap of M scales as 1/L3/2 for large enough
|s|, it would imply that the dynamical exponent of the large deviations of activity in the SSEP is 3 /2 for
deviations beyond the diﬀusive regime (where the dynamical exponent is 2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites: each site is occupied by at most one particle, and every particle attempts to jump to each neighboring site with rate 1, the move being executed only if the target site is empty. The activity over a time window is defined as the total number of particle jumps (in either direction) performed during that window. Tilting the continuous-time Markov generator by a parameter s conjugate to the activity yields the deformed (non-stochastic) matrix M(s), whose largest eigenvalue gives the scaled cumulant generating function of the activity and whose subleading spectral gap Δ_M(L,s) controls finite-time relaxation of activity-biased trajectories.

Consider also the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on a ring of L sites with biased hopping rates, and the deformed generator W(s') obtained by tilting with a parameter s' conjugate to the integrated particle current. There exists a similarity/parameter mapping that identifies the spectra of M(s) (SSEP, activity-biased) and W(s') (ASEP, current-biased) outside the diffusive regime.

Questions:
(1) Can the spectral gap of the deformed evolution operators M(s) and W(s') be computed by the Bethe Ansatz in the vicinity of dynamical phase transitions and at nonzero values of the Legendre conjugate parameter s (respectively s')?
(2) Using the mapping between M and W, does the gap of M(s) satisfy
   Δ_M(L,s) ~ C(s) · L^{-3/2}  as L → ∞,
for all sufficiently large |s|, thereby establishing that the dynamical exponent governing SSEP activity large deviations beyond the diffusive regime equals 3/2 (in contrast with the value 2 of the diffusive regime)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction: while Bethe Ansatz computations of gaps for ASEP at s=0 are classical and give the KPZ exponent 3/2, extending such gap computations to the deformed (s≠0) activity-tilted SSEP generator near dynamical phase transitions, and rigorously establishing Δ_M(L,s) ~ L^{-3/2} for large |s|, does not appear to have been carried out in the literature. Related works on tensor-network sampling of activity large deviations and on KPZ regimes in SSEP activity statistics are consistent with the conjecture but do not prove the claimed gap scaling.

status_evidence.title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes
status_evidence.snippet: States that a 1/L^{3/2} gap in the deformed matrix M for SSEP activity would imply a dynamical exponent 3/2 for large |s|, and lists Bethe-Ansatz study of the deformed gap as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The gap scaling and Bethe-Ansatz computation are explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Optimal sampling of dynamical large deviations in two dimensions via tensor networks
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical/tensor-network approaches to activity large deviations of exclusion processes, no rigorous gap result for deformed SSEP.
status_evidence.claim: Recent numerical work does not settle the analytic gap scaling question.
